data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction is a category error in the context of append-only logs: idempotency and safety are properties of operations, but the append-only log requires a property of the delivery protocol\u2014namely, that retried writes are distinguishable from original writes by the replay layer. This 'distinguishability' is neither idempotency nor safety; it is a protocol-level invariant that the log enforces through metadata (delivery IDs, producer epochs, sequence numbers). The writers need only attach this metadata; they need not themselves be idempotent or safe.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the replay layer ignores delivery metadata and relies solely on content comparison, then distinguishability reduces to content idempotency and this framing collapses","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log has no mechanism for attaching metadata (raw append of opaque bytes), then the protocol-level invariant cannot be enforced and the log falls back to requiring content-level idempotency","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If one defines 'safe' broadly enough to include 'attaches metadata that enables downstream deduplication,' then the log does require safe writers under this broad definition","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The real requirement is that the replay layer can tell which entries are duplicates of which. This is a protocol property (delivery metadata), not an operation property (idempotency/safety). A writer that attaches a unique delivery ID to each attempt is neither idempotent (different IDs per attempt) nor formally safe (it has side effects), but the replay layer can collapse entries with matching logical keys. The confusion arises from conflating operation-level properties with protocol-level guarantees.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
